_meta.indication: ANKTIVA in combination with BCG is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, three-cohort, multicenter, uncontrolled trial; patients with CIS were enrolled into Cohort A (N-803 with BCG).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS with or without papillary tumors (Cohort A).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was complete response (CR) rate at any time (per local pathology/investigator); duration of response was a secondary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: FDA efficacy population of 77 patients with BCG-unresponsive CIS (88 patients enrolled into Cohort A).
pivotal_trials.result: CR rate at any time (per local pathology, FDA efficacy population of 77) was 62.3% (95% CI: 50.6, 73.1); median duration of response 45.4 months (95% CI 19.9, NE), with 58.3% having duration ≥ 12 months.

key_safety: Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions were increased creatinine, dysuria (32%), hematuria (32%), urinary frequency (27%), micturition urgency (25%), urinary tract infection (24%), increased potassium, musculoskeletal pain (17%), chills (15%) and pyrexia (15%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 16% of patients; a fatal cardiac arrest occurred in 1 (1.1%) patient.
target_moa: Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln is an IL-15 receptor agonist; given as a boost to the trained immunity induced by BCG (prime), it generates memory T cells and memory NK cells with enhanced efficacy and durable response.
modality: Other – recombinant fusion protein complex (IL-15 superagonist): nogapendekin alfa (IL-15N72D variant) bound to inbakicept (IL-15Rα sushi domain/IgG1 Fc fusion protein).
companion_dx_detail: The Applicant did not submit an application for an in vitro diagnostic device; FDA agreed use of an IVD is not essential to the safe and effective use of the drug.

advisory_committee.vote: No oncologic drug advisory committee (ODAC) discussion or consultations external to the FDA were deemed necessary for this application.

summary.text: ANKTIVA received regular (standard) approval as a BLA under section 351(a), supported by the single-arm QUILT-3.032 trial. The program had Fast Track (2017) and Breakthrough Therapy (2019) designations; the initial BLA received a Complete Response (May 9, 2023) for product quality issues, and the resubmission led to regular approval with a postmarketing commitment to complete QUILT-3.032 and provide duration-of-response updates.

requirement.text: 4417-1 Complete clinical trial "QUILT-3.032: A Multicenter Clinical Trial of Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) in Combination With ALT-803 (N-803) in Patients With BCG Unresponsive High Grade Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer," and provide annual updates on enrollment, complete response rate, and duration of response for all patients enrolled in Cohort 1 (non-muscle invasive bladder cancer [NMIBC] carcinoma in situ [CIS]). requirement.text: 4417-5 Continue studies to re-validate the ADA and NAb immunogenicity assays using a more suitable positive control, such as an anti-N-803 affinity purified antibody. To support the use of this positive control, validation data should be provided to demonstrate that the positive control can sufficiently bind to all domains of N-803 (e.g., IL-15 variant, IL-15Rα domain, and IgG1 Fc domain) with adequate sensitivity or additional positive controls (e.g., domain-specific N-803 positive controls) may be needed to supplement your validation approach. Submit the final assay validation reports to the BLA.
